## Detector false positives - per-finding evidence

This is the evidence for the "no detector exemptions were needed" claim.
Every symbol below was reported dead by the widened scan and is in fact
live. The generator asks the SAME reference graph the gate asks and prints
the real call site it finds, so the claim is re-checked on every run rather
than asserted. If one of these ever loses its caller, regeneration fails
instead of leaving a stale line here.

| False positive | Declared at | Caller(s) found by the gate's reference graph | Root cause |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AnrWatchdog.isMainThreadResponsive` | `android/app/src/main/java/com/scmessenger/android/service/AnrWatchdog.kt:260` | called from android/app/src/main/java/com/scmessenger/android/service/AnrWatchdog.kt:204 | 1 - override/private functions were invisible as scopes - buildAnrDiagnostics is private, so the call was attributed to the nearest preceding tracked declaration and lost. |
| `MeshRepository.getMeshService` | `android/app/src/main/java/com/scmessenger/android/data/MeshRepository.kt:4210` | called from android/app/src/main/java/com/scmessenger/android/service/MeshSyncWorker.kt:36 | 1 - override/private functions were invisible as scopes - once getMeshRepository was mis-called dead, this became C4 transitively dead through it. |
| `MeshSyncWorkerEntryPoint.getMeshRepository` | `android/app/src/main/java/com/scmessenger/android/service/MeshSyncWorker.kt:25` | called from android/app/src/main/java/com/scmessenger/android/service/MeshSyncWorker.kt:35 | 1 - override/private functions were invisible as scopes - doWork is an override, so it was never a tracked scope and the call inside it was discarded as a self-reference. |
| `SmartTransportRouter.getPreferredTransport` | `android/app/src/main/java/com/scmessenger/android/transport/SmartTransportRouter.kt:174` | called from android/app/src/main/java/com/scmessenger/android/transport/SmartTransportRouter.kt:370 | 2 - line proximity cannot model nesting - attemptDelivery declares data class TransportAttempt inside its own body, which masked the enclosing function. |

## Root causes

1. **`override` and `private` functions were invisible as scopes.**

They are deliberately not reachability targets, so they are not collected -

but the reference map also used them to decide which scope a line sits in. A

call inside an `override` or `private` body was attributed to the nearest

preceding tracked declaration and then discarded as a self-reference.



Fix: `collect_scope_ranges` records brace-depth ranges for every class AND

function, including the untracked ones, and a line is attributed to the

smallest range containing it.

2. **Line proximity cannot model nesting.**

`SmartTransportRouter` declares `data class TransportAttempt` *inside* the

function `attemptDelivery`, so "nearest preceding declaration" picked the

inner class for lines the function actually contains.

3. **A class whose opening brace is on a later line was dropped.**

`open class MeshRepository(` (line 55) and `class AnrWatchdog(` (line 29)

have no opening brace on their own line, so the class never entered the scope

stack and every fqcn inside it lost the class name. That turned live calls

into apparent external callers and mis-scored whole classes.



Fix: the declaration is deferred and pushed when its brace appears, matching

the original extractor's `pending_class` handling.



This one was caught by re-checking every resolution against the source rather

than trusting the detector, after a first attempt at the fix silently

mis-scored live methods.

Self-detection also had to stop comparing names alone. An anonymous
`object : Callback { override fun onStartSuccess() }` computes the same
qualified name as the outer method it delegates to, so `this@Outer.m()` would
look recursive. The scope's start line is compared instead.

## Checks performed before classifying anything

- `src/test` and `src/androidTest` are outside the reference corpus, so no test caller can make a function look wired to production.
- Zero `.java` sources under `android/`, so there is no Java caller the scan misses.
- No reflective string invocation of any flagged symbol.
- No flagged symbol is an `override`, an implemented interface member, an `@EntryPoint` accessor, or a serialization hook - so none of them qualifies for a detector exemption. Every exemption route was available and none was needed. The false-positive table above is the per-finding proof, re-derived on each run.
- The detector scans `android/app/src/main` only. `android/shared/` and `shared/` are outside the corpus. Checked explicitly: none of the 32 findings was referenced from those roots. Recorded as a known limitation rather than silently ignored.

Still `--method-findings=warn`, deliberately. The remaining findings need product decisions, not a policy change: each is either a feature that should be wired or code that should go. Once those are resolved, promoting is a one-word change.
